title: 30 Prayer Journal Ideas for Beginners (With Layouts)
description: 30 simple prayer journal ideas for beginners: page layouts, prayer lists, verse pages and answered prayer trackers. Try any of them free right on this page.
h1: 30 prayer journal ideas for beginners and beyond
intro: The best prayer journal ideas are simple: a weekly prayer list, a page for answered prayers, a verse page, and a short daily entry using a method like ACTS. Below are 30 ideas sorted into page layouts, prayer lists, Bible pages and creative ideas, with tips on which ones to try first.

sections.h2: Prayer journal ideas for beginners: start here

blocks.p: If you are new, do not try all 30 ideas at once. Pick three and use them for a month. Most people find that these three are enough to build a steady habit:

ol: **A short daily entry.** Date, one verse, a few lines of prayer. Use the [prayer journal template](/prayer-journal-template/) if you want boxes to fill in.
**A prayer list.** Names and needs in one place so you never forget who you promised to pray for.
**An answered prayers page.** Every time God answers, write it down with the date.

blocks.p: Once those feel easy, add one new idea at a time. A prayer journal grows with you. It does not have to look finished on day one.

sections.h2: Prayer journal page ideas and layouts

blocks.p: These are ways to set up a single page or a two page spread.

ol: **ACTS page.** Four boxes: Adoration, Confession, Thanksgiving, Supplication. See the full [ACTS prayer journal](/prayer-journal-acts/) guide.
**SOAP page.** Scripture, Observation, Application, Prayer. Good if your prayer time starts in the Bible.
**Split page.** Left side for requests, right side left blank for answers you fill in later.
**Weekly spread.** Seven small boxes, one per day, with a line or two of prayer in each.
**Monthly overview.** A calendar page where you color in each day you prayed. It shows your habit at a glance.
**Letter to God.** No boxes at all. Start with Dear Father and write like a letter.
**Prayer of the month.** One big need written at the top of the month, with notes added as the weeks go by.
**Three line page.** Thank You for, I am sorry for, Please help with. Perfect for busy days.

blocks.p: A prayer list keeps you faithful to the people you care about. Here are ways to organize one.

ol: **Prayer list by day.** Family on Monday, church on Tuesday, friends on Wednesday, work on Thursday, the world on Friday, your own heart on the weekend.
**Inner circle and outer circle.** A short list you pray for every day, and a longer list you pray for once a week.
**Prayer cards.** One index card per person with their needs and verses. Keep them in a box and pray through a few each day.
**People who do not know Jesus.** A page of names you are praying will come to faith.
**Leaders.** Pastors, teachers, bosses, and government leaders, each with one specific request.
**Hard people.** A short, honest list of people who hurt you, where you choose to pray for them anyway.
**Long term prayers.** Needs you have prayed about for years. Date them so you remember how long you have waited.
**Verse of the week.** Write one verse at the top of a page and pray it in your own words each day.
**Promises page.** A list of God's promises you want to remember, with the reference for each.
**Pray a psalm.** Read a psalm line by line and write your own prayer after each line.
**Names of God.** One page per name, like Shepherd, Provider or Prince of Peace, with what it means to you.
**Prayers of the Bible.** Study a prayer from Scripture, like Hannah's or Paul's, then write one like it.
**Sermon notes to prayer.** After church, write one point from the sermon and turn it into a prayer.
**Memory verse tracker.** Write a verse you are learning by heart, then check a box each day you say it from memory.

blocks.p: For more on this, see [how to journal the Bible](/how-to-journal-the-bible/) and these [Bible journal prompts](/bible-journal-prompts/).

ol: **Gratitude jar page.** Draw a jar and fill it with small words of thanks through the month.
**Prayer map.** Draw a simple map of your street, city or the world and write prayers on it.
**Color code.** One color for praise, one for requests, one for answers.
**Photo prayers.** Tape in a photo of someone you love and write a prayer around it.
**One word for the year.** Pick a word like trust or rest and write about it each month.
**Prayer walk notes.** Take a walk while you pray, then write what you saw and prayed for.
**Letters to your children or spouse.** Write prayers you may share with them one day. See the [prayer journal for your children](/prayer-journal-for-your-children/).
**Year end review.** On the last page of the year, list every answered prayer you can find.

blocks.tip: Pretty is optional. A plain notebook and a pen work just as well as stickers and washi tape. Use the creative ideas only if they help you pray, not if they become a reason to skip praying.

sections.h2: An example page using these ideas

blocks.p: Here is a simple daily entry that mixes the three line page with a verse of the week.

example.label: Prayer journal
example.title: Dear Father,
example.text:
Verse of the week: Psalm 46:10
Thank You for a calm morning and coffee with Mom.
I am sorry for snapping at the kids before school.
Please help Jen with her test results on Friday.
Help me be still today instead of rushing.
Prayer list (Wednesday): friends. Amy, Lisa, Grace.

blocks.p: You can find more filled in pages in our [prayer journal examples](/prayer-journal-examples/).

sections.h2: Tips for keeping your prayer journal going

ul: **Tie it to something you already do.** Pray with your morning coffee or right after you put the kids to bed.
**Keep it where you see it.** On the kitchen table or next to your Bible, not in a drawer.
**Lower the bar.** On hard days, one line counts.
**Use prompts when you are stuck.** Our list of [prayer journal prompts](/prayer-journal-prompts/) has over 100.

**Go digital if paper does not stick.** You can write on this page, or try the [Prayer Journal for Women](/prayer-journal-for-women/) Android app, coming soon on Google Play, which has a prayer list, answered prayers, reminders and 52 weeks of verses.
**Celebrate answers.** Reading your answered prayers page is the best fuel to keep going.

faq.q: What should I put in my prayer journal?
faq.a: Most prayer journals have a few parts: the date, a Bible verse, written prayers of praise and thanks, a list of people and needs, and a place to record answered prayers. You can add a verse page, a list of God's promises, or sermon notes. Start with the basics and add more only if it helps you pray.

faq.q: How do I organize my prayer journal?
faq.a: A simple way is to use tabs or sections: daily entries in the front, a prayer list in the middle, and answered prayers at the back. Some people organize their prayer list by day of the week so every group gets prayed for once a week without feeling overwhelming.

faq.q: What are good prayer journal ideas for beginners?
faq.a: Start with three things: a short daily entry, a prayer list, and an answered prayers page. The three line page, with Thank You for, I am sorry for, and Please help with, is the easiest place to begin. Add other ideas once those feel natural.

faq.q: Do I need a special notebook for a prayer journal?
faq.a: No. Any notebook works, and so does a page on your phone or computer. Some people like a dedicated journal because it feels set apart for God. What matters is that you can find it easily and use it often.

faq.q: How often should I write in my prayer journal?
faq.a: There is no rule in Scripture about how often to journal. Many people write a few lines most days. Others write once a week and pray without writing on the other days. Pick a rhythm you can actually keep.
